description: Savor the true taste of the Italian coast with this exquisite Spaghetti alle Vongole featuring tender Manila clams. This classic dish combines al dente spaghetti with a light, flavorful sauce of garlic, white wine, and fresh parsley, creating a perfectly balanced seafood pasta experience. It is a simple yet elegant meal that transports you straight to a seaside trattoria.

instructions.title: Prepare Clams and Ingredients
instructions.text: Begin by purging the Manila clams. Place them in a large bowl of cold salted water (about 1 tablespoon of salt per liter of water) for at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 hours. This helps them expel any sand. Discard any clams that are open and do not close when tapped. Finely slice the garlic and chop the fresh parsley.

instructions.title: Start the Sauce Base
instructions.text: In a large skillet or wide pot, heat the extra virgin olive oil over medium heat. Add the sliced garlic and, if using, the red pepper flakes. Sauté gently until the garlic is fragrant and lightly golden, about 2-3 minutes. Be careful not to burn the garlic.

instructions.title: Cook the Spaghetti
instructions.text: While the garlic is infusing, bring a large pot of generously salted water to a rolling boil. Add the spaghetti and cook according to package directions until al dente, usually about 8-10 minutes. Reserve about 1 cup of the starchy pasta cooking water before draining the spaghetti.

instructions.title: Steam the Clams
instructions.text: Increase the heat under the skillet with the garlic to medium-high. Add the purged and drained Manila clams to the skillet, then pour in the dry white wine. Cover the skillet tightly with a lid and cook for 3-5 minutes, shaking the pan occasionally, until all the clams have opened. Discard any clams that do not open.

instructions.title: Combine Pasta and Clams
instructions.text: Add the al dente spaghetti directly into the skillet with the opened clams and their liquid. Add half of the chopped fresh parsley. Toss everything together vigorously to combine, allowing the pasta to absorb the flavorful clam broth. If the sauce seems too dry, add a splash of the reserved pasta cooking water to create a silky emulsion.

instructions.title: Finish and Serve
instructions.text: Continue to toss the pasta and clams for another minute or two, ensuring the spaghetti is well coated. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and freshly ground black pepper as needed. Serve immediately in warm bowls, garnished with the remaining fresh chopped parsley. A drizzle of fresh extra virgin olive oil over each serving is a delightful finish.

tips: Always purge your clams thoroughly. Soaking them in cold, salted water ensures a grit-free, enjoyable experience, which is fundamental for authentic Vongole.
Do not overcook the clams; they will become tough. As soon as they open, they are ready. Remove any that remain closed after a few minutes of steaming.
The starchy pasta water is your secret weapon. Use it to emulsify the sauce, creating a richer, more cohesive coating for your spaghetti without adding extra fat.
